items.stem: Meena and Hari observed an animal in their garden. Hari called it an insect while Meena said it was an earthworm. Choose the correct option which confirms that it is an insect. (i) Bilateral symmetrical body (ii) Body with jointed legs (iii) Cylindrical body (iv) Body with little segmentation
items.answer: Option (ii) Body with jointed legs. Insects belong to the phylum Arthropoda, and the defining structural feature of arthropods is the presence of jointed appendages (legs), distinguishing them from earthworms which belong to Annelida.

items.stem: Sponges represent one of the simplest animal body plans. Their bodies lack true tissues and organs. Which feature of sponge cells supports its classification under the animal kingdom? (i) Absence of mitochondria (ii) Ability to photosynthesise (iii) Presence of a cell membrane (iv) Presence of a cell wall
items.answer: Option (iii) Presence of a cell membrane. Animal cells are eukaryotic and, unlike plants and fungi, they lack a rigid cell wall, meaning their outer boundary is solely the cell membrane.

items.stem: Observe two different animals in your immediate environment. What features help you distinguish between them? How do these features help place them into different groups?
items.answer: If we observe a bird (like a pigeon) and an earthworm in our environment, we can distinguish them by several visible structural features. The bird possesses feathers, wings, an internal skeleton with a backbone, and well-developed sensory organs, whereas the earthworm has a cylindrical, segmented body with no internal skeleton or limbs. These distinct features help classify them accurately: the earthworm is placed under Invertebrates (Phylum Annelida) due to Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification 6.
